items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: I taught Teddy... I started off like he did... he was about the only one could do at that time

ctx.x: Can you demonstrate, Chuck, for us some of the kind of tap dancing that these artists did?

Yes. Yes. Say, for instance now, Teddy Hale tapped danced, and I started off like he did, you know. It's the way I taught Teddy (inaudible). I mean, You have to ask yourself the compromises. Okay. I'll compromise (inaudible). (Mr. Green demonstrates some tap dancing steps.)

That's some of Teddy Hale. Well, he was doing improvising. He was being musical, see. If some song was happening like he would call it "Blue Skies," you know. He liked that piece, you know, to practice on, you see. But if he danced a capella -- by himself, you know -- he started out (unintelligible) you know, the falling of his heels. How to fall the heels. Let them come down, you know, and go away, and the raising of the heels, and so forth, into the toes, you see.
